title: Super Triple 2 (NSIC Rc 222) Inbred Rice: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Super Triple 2 (NSIC Rc 222) Rice: Yield and Maturity
metaDescription: Super Triple 2 is NSIC Rc 222, an inbred rice for irrigated lowland: about 114 days and 6.1 tonnes per hectare on average. See its ratings.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 222 is an inbred rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as Super Triple 2 or Super Triple Two and known locally as Tubigan 18. The NSIC approved it in 2009. IRRI bred it. It matures in about 114 days and averages 6.1 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 10 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 222 yield?

On average it gives 6.1 tonnes per hectare. That is about 122 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits above the average of the 118 irrigated lowland inbreds on the list, which is 5.2 tonnes. But the top yield, 10 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 114 days from sowing to harvest, and about 106 days if you seed it directly. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With intermediate amylose, expect rice that is soft but not sticky. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is Super Triple 2 the same as NSIC Rc 222?
items.a: Yes. Super Triple 2 is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 222 is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Tubigan 18. The numbers on this page are for NSIC Rc 222.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 222?
items.a: It is known as Tubigan 18. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 222 take to harvest?
items.a: About 114 days after sowing when transplanted, and about 106 days when direct seeded. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 222?
items.a: It averages 6.1 tonnes per hectare, about 122 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 10 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
